name: Chapter 11: Three Dimensional Geometry
description: Direction cosines and ratios, equations of a line in vector and Cartesian form, angle between lines, shortest distance between skew and parallel lines, with exam-style problems.

cards.term: Direction cosines of a line?
cards.definition: The cosines of the angles α, β, γ the line makes with the positive x, y, z axes: l = cos α, m = cos β, n = cos γ, with l² + m² + n² = 1

cards.term: Direction cosines of the three coordinate axes?
cards.definition: x-axis (1, 0, 0), y-axis (0, 1, 0), z-axis (0, 0, 1) (Example 4: angles 0°, 90°, 90°)

cards.term: Reversed direction: what happens to the direction cosines?
cards.definition: All three change sign: (−l, −m, −n) (angles become π − α, π − β, π − γ). So a line has two sets of direction cosines

cards.term: Direction ratios: definition and link to direction cosines.
cards.definition: Any numbers a, b, c proportional to (l, m, n). Then l = a/√(a² + b² + c²), m = b/√(...), n = c/√(...) (with ± for the two directions)

cards.term: Direction cosines and direction ratios of a line
cards.definition: Direction cosines l,m,n = cosines of angles with the axes; l^2+m^2+n^2 = 1; direction ratios a,b,c proportional to l,m,n: l = a/sqrt(a^2+b^2+c^2); axes have (1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Direction cosines

A line makes angles α, β, γ with the positive x, y, z axes. For the line through O and P(2, 3, 4) find its direction cosines and show l² + m² + n² = 1.

Divide the coordinates of P by |OP|.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Direction cosines

A line makes angles α, β, γ with the positive x, y, z axes. For the line through O and P(2, 3, 4) find its direction cosines and show l² + m² + n² = 1.

Direction cosines l = cos α, m = cos β, n = cos γ. For OP: l = x/|OP| = 2/√29, m = 3/√29, n = 4/√29. They are the components of the unit vector along the line, so l² + m² + n² = 1 (4 + 9 + 16 = 29).

Direction ratios a, b, c are any numbers proportional to (l, m, n): l = a/√(a² + b² + c²), etc. The axes have direction cosines (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (0, 0, 1) (Example 4). Reversing the direction changes all three signs.

cards.term: Direction ratios of the line through P(x₁, y₁, z₁) and Q(x₂, y₂, z₂)?
cards.definition: x₂ − x₁, y₂ − y₁, z₂ − z₁ (and dividing by PQ gives the direction cosines)

cards.term: Example 1: a line makes 90°, 60°, 30° with the x, y, z axes. Its direction cosines?
Example 2: direction ratios 2, −1, −2. Direction cosines?
cards.definition: Magnitude √(4 + 1 + 4) = 3: (2/3, −1/3, −2/3)

cards.term: Example 5: A(2, 3, −4), B(1, −2, 3), C(3, 8, −11): show they are collinear.
cards.definition: AB has ratios (−1, −5, 7) and BC has (2, 10, −14) = −2 × (−1, −5, 7). Proportional and B is common: collinear

cards.term: Trap: are the direction cosines of a line unique?
cards.definition: No: (l, m, n) and (−l, −m, −n) both describe the line (opposite directions), and direction ratios can be scaled by any non-zero factor

cards.term: If a line makes equal angles with the axes, its direction cosines are?
cards.definition: l = m = n with 3l² = 1: ±(1/√3, 1/√3, 1/√3) (angle cos⁻¹(1/√3) ≈ 54.7°)

cards.term: Can a line make angles 30°, 45°, 60° with the three axes?
cards.definition: cos²30° + cos²45° + cos²60° = 3/4 + 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/2 ≠ 1: No

cards.term: Ex 11.1 Q1: a line makes 90°, 135°, 45° with the x, y, z axes. Find its direction cosines.
Ex 11.1 Q2: direction cosines of a line making equal angles with the axes.
Ex 11.1 Q3: direction ratios −18, 12, −4. Direction cosines?

cards.definition: Ratios of the first two: (−3, −5, −3). Of the last two: (6, 10, 6) = −2(−3, −5, −3). Collinear

cards.term: Ex 11.1 Q5: direction cosines of the sides of the triangle with vertices (3, 5, −4), (−1, 1, 2), (−5, −5, −2).
Vector and Cartesian equations of a line
cards.definition: Line through a parallel to b: r = a + lambda b; Cartesian (x-x1)/a = (y-y1)/b = (z-z1)/c; through two points use b = a2 - a1

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Equation of a line in space

Write the vector equation of the line through the point A (position vector a) parallel to the vector b. What is its Cartesian form?

Move from A along b by any multiple λ.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Equation of a line in space

Write the vector equation of the line through the point A (position vector a) parallel to the vector b. What is its Cartesian form?

A point P on the line satisfies AP = λb for some real λ, so r = a + λ b (λ ∈ R). If a = (x₁, y₁, z₁) and b = (a, b, c) then x = x₁ + λa, y = y₁ + λb, z = z₁ + λc; eliminating λ gives (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c.

Through two points a, a′: direction b = a′ − a. If the direction cosines l, m, n are used, write l, m, n in place of a, b, c. (Example 6: through (5, 2, −4) parallel to 3î + 2ĵ − 8k̂.)

cards.term: Vector equation of the line through the point a parallel to b?
cards.definition: r = a + λ b (λ ∈ R). Here r is the position vector of a general point of the line

cards.term: Cartesian equation of the line through (x₁, y₁, z₁) with direction ratios a, b, c?
cards.definition: (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c. If a denominator is 0, that numerator is 0 (e.g. x/1 = y/0 = z/0 is the x-axis)

cards.term: Line through two points a and a′?
cards.definition: Direction is a′ − a: r = a + λ(a′ − a); Cartesian (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (z − z₁)/(z₂ − z₁)

cards.term: Conversion between vector and Cartesian forms.
cards.definition:
r = (x₁î + y₁ĵ + z₁k̂) + λ(aî + bĵ + ck̂) ⇔ (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c.
Read a point and the direction ratios off either form

cards.term: Example 6: line through (5, 2, −4) parallel to 3î + 2ĵ − 8k̂. Vector and Cartesian equations.
cards.definition: r = 5î + 2ĵ − 4k̂ + λ(3î + 2ĵ − 8k̂) and (x − 5)/3 = (y − 2)/2 = (z + 4)/(−8)

cards.term: Parametric equations of a line: what are they?
cards.definition: x = x₁ + λa, y = y₁ + λb, z = z₁ + λc: every value of λ gives a point of the line. They are handy for finding intersections and distances

cards.term: Trap: is the direction of the line (x − 1)/2 = (y + 3)/(−1) = (z − 4)/5 the vector (1, −3, 4)?
cards.definition: No: (1, −3, 4) is a point on the line. The direction ratios are the denominators: (2, −1, 5)

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q4: the line through (1, 2, 3) parallel to 3î + 2ĵ − 2k̂.
cards.definition: r = î + 2ĵ + 3k̂ + λ(3î + 2ĵ − 2k̂) or (x − 1)/3 = (y − 2)/2 = (z − 3)/(−2)

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q5: the line (vector and Cartesian) through the point 2î − ĵ + 4k̂ in the direction î + 2ĵ − k̂.
cards.definition: r = 2î − ĵ + 4k̂ + λ(î + 2ĵ − k̂) and (x − 2)/1 = (y + 1)/2 = (z − 4)/(−1)

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q6: the Cartesian equation of the line through (−2, 4, −5) parallel to (x + 3)/3 = (y − 4)/5 = (z + 8)/6.
cards.definition: Parallel lines share direction ratios (3, 5, 6): (x + 2)/3 = (y − 4)/5 = (z + 5)/6

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q7: the Cartesian equation (x − 5)/3 = (y + 4)/7 = (z − 6)/2. Write its vector form.
cards.definition: Point (5, −4, 6), direction (3, 7, 2): r = 5î − 4ĵ + 6k̂ + λ(3î + 7ĵ + 2k̂)

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q1: show the three lines with direction cosines (12/13, −3/13, −4/13), (4/13, 12/13, 3/13), (3/13, −4/13, 12/13) are mutually perpendicular.
cards.definition: Dot products: 12·4 − 3·12 − 4·3 = 0, 4·3 + 12(−4) + 3·12 = 0, 12·3 + (−3)(−4) + (−4)(12) = 0 (each over 169). Mutually perpendicular

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q2: show the line through (1, −1, 2), (3, 4, −2) is perpendicular to the line through (0, 3, 2), (3, 5, 6).
cards.definition: Directions (2, 5, −4) and (3, 2, 4): 6 + 10 − 16 = 0. Perpendicular

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q3: show the line through (4, 7, 8), (2, 3, 4) is parallel to the line through (−1, −2, 1), (1, 2, 5).
cards.definition: Directions (−2, −4, −4) and (2, 4, 4): proportional (ratio −1). Parallel

cards.term: Angle between two lines from direction ratios
cards.definition: cos(theta) = |a1a2+b1b2+c1c2| / (sqrt(a1^2+b1^2+c1^2) sqrt(a2^2+b2^2+c2^2)); perpendicular when the dot product is zero; parallel when ratios are proportional

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Angle between two lines

How do you find the angle between two lines from their direction ratios (a₁, b₁, c₁) and (a₂, b₂, c₂)?

Use the direction vectors of the lines.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Angle between two lines

How do you find the angle between two lines from their direction ratios (a₁, b₁, c₁) and (a₂, b₂, c₂)?

The angle between two lines (even skew ones) is the angle between their direction vectors: cos θ = |a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂| / (√(a₁² + b₁² + c₁²) √(a₂² + b₂² + c₂²)), with θ acute. With direction cosines: cos θ = |l₁l₂ + m₁m₂ + n₁n₂|.

Perpendicular ⇔ a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0; parallel ⇔ a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. (Ex 11.2 Q8(i): directions (3, 2, 6) and (1, 2, 2) give cos θ = 19/21.)

cards.term: Angle between two lines with direction cosines (l₁, m₁, n₁) and (l₂, m₂, n₂)?
cards.definition: cos θ = |l₁l₂ + m₁m₂ + n₁n₂| (θ acute). With direction ratios divide by both magnitudes

cards.term: Conditions for two lines to be perpendicular / parallel?
cards.definition: Perpendicular: a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0. Parallel: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

cards.term: Angle between lines r = a₁ + λb₁ and r = a₂ + μb₂ in vector form?
cards.definition: cos θ = |b₁ · b₂|/(|b₁||b₂|)

cards.term: Angle between lines with direction ratios (1, 1, 2) and (1, 1, 0)?
cards.definition: dot = 2, magnitudes √6 and √2: cos θ = 2/√12 = 1/√3, so θ = cos⁻¹(1/√3)

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q8(i): angle between r = 2î − 5ĵ + k̂ + λ(3î + 2ĵ + 6k̂) and r = 7î − 6k̂ + μ(î + 2ĵ + 2k̂).
cards.definition: b₁ · b₂ = 19, |b₁| = 7, |b₂| = 3: cos θ = 19/21. θ = cos⁻¹(19/21)

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q8(ii): angle between r = 3î + ĵ − 2k̂ + λ(î − ĵ − 2k̂) and r = 2î − ĵ − 56k̂ + μ(3î − 5ĵ − 4k̂).

cards.definition: Directions (2, 5, −3), (−1, 8, 4): dot = 26, magnitudes √38 and 9: θ = cos⁻¹(26/(9√38))

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q9(ii): angle between x/2 = y/2 = z/1 and (x − 5)/4 = (y − 2)/1 = (z − 3)/8.
cards.definition: Directions (2, 2, 1), (4, 1, 8): dot = 18, magnitudes 3 and 9: θ = cos⁻¹(2/3)

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q10: find p so the lines (1 − x)/3 = (7y − 14)/(2p) = (z − 3)/2 and (7 − 7x)/(3p) = (y − 5)/1 = (6 − z)/5 are perpendicular.
cards.definition: Rewrite to standard form: direction ratios (−3, 2p/7, 2) and (−3p/7, 1, −5). Dot = 9p/7 + 2p/7 − 10 = 0: p = 70/11

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q11: show (x − 5)/7 = (y + 2)/(−5) = z/1 and x/1 = y/2 = z/3 are perpendicular.
cards.definition: Directions (7, −5, 1) and (1, 2, 3): 7 − 10 + 3 = 0 ✓

cards.term: What are skew lines?
cards.definition: Two lines in space that are neither parallel nor intersecting (they do not lie in one plane)

cards.term: Angle between skew lines?
cards.definition:
The angle between two intersecting lines drawn through any point (often the origin) parallel to each.
It equals the angle between the direction vectors

cards.term: Shortest distance between two skew lines
cards.definition: Skew lines: d = |(a2-a1).(b1 x b2)|/|b1 x b2|; parallel lines: |b x (a2-a1)|/|b|; d = 0 means the lines are coplanar/intersect; common perpendicular parallel to b1 x b2

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Shortest distance between skew lines

Two lines are neither parallel nor intersecting (skew lines). What is the shortest distance between them?

Project a₂ − a₁ onto the direction perpendicular to both lines.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Shortest distance between skew lines

Two lines are neither parallel nor intersecting (skew lines). What is the shortest distance between them?

The shortest distance is along the common perpendicular, which is parallel to b₁ × b₂. For l₁: r = a₁ + λb₁ and l₂: r = a₂ + μb₂: d = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂| (the projection of a₂ − a₁ on the common perpendicular).

If l₁ ∥ l₂ (b₁ ∥ b₂), the distance is instead |b × (a₂ − a₁)|/|b| (Example 10). d = 0 means the lines intersect (coplanar).

cards.term: Distance between skew lines r = a₁ + λb₁ and r = a₂ + μb₂?
cards.definition: d = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂|

cards.term: Distance between parallel lines r = a₁ + λb and r = a₂ + μb?
cards.definition: d = |b × (a₂ − a₁)| / |b|

cards.term: Cartesian form of the skew-lines distance.
cards.definition: For (x − x₁)/a₁ = (y − y₁)/b₁ = (z − z₁)/c₁ and (x − x₂)/a₂ = ...: d = |det[x₂ − x₁, y₂ − y₁, z₂ − z₁; a₁ b₁ c₁; a₂ b₂ c₂]| / √((b₁c₂ − b₂c₁)² + (c₁a₂ − c₂a₁)² + (a₁b₂ − a₂b₁)²)

cards.term: How can you tell whether two lines are coplanar (intersect or are parallel)?
cards.definition: The shortest distance is 0 (scalar triple product (a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂) = 0)

cards.term: Example 10: distance between the parallel lines through a₁ = î + 2ĵ − 4k̂ and a₂ = 3î + 3ĵ − 5k̂, both with b = 2î + 3ĵ + 6k̂.
cards.definition: a₂ − a₁ = (2, 1, −1); b × (a₂ − a₁) = (−9, 14, −4), magnitude √293; |b| = 7: d = √293/7

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q12: shortest distance between r = (î + 2ĵ + k̂) + λ(î − ĵ + k̂) and r = 2î − ĵ − k̂ + μ(2î + ĵ + 2k̂).
Ex 11.2 Q14: shortest distance between r = (î + 2ĵ + 3k̂) + λ(î − 3ĵ + 2k̂) and r = 4î + 5ĵ + 6k̂ + μ(2î + 3ĵ + k̂).
cards.definition: b₁ × b₂ = (-9, 3, 9), |b₁ × b₂| = 3√19, numerator 9: d = 3/√19

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q15: shortest distance between r = (1 − t)î + (t − 2)ĵ + (3 − 2t)k̂ and r = (s + 1)î + (2s − 1)ĵ − (2s + 1)k̂.
cards.definition: Line 1: a₁ = î − 2ĵ + 3k̂, b₁ = −î + ĵ − 2k̂. Line 2: a₂ = î − ĵ − k̂, b₂ = î + 2ĵ − 2k̂. b₁ × b₂ = (2, −4, −3), |b₁ × b₂| = √29, and (a₂ − a₁) = (0, 1, −4) gives (a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂) = 8. d = 8/√29

cards.term: Misc Q1: the angle between lines with direction ratios a, b, c and b − c, c − a, a − b.
cards.definition: Dot product: a(b − c) + b(c − a) + c(a − b) = ab − ac + bc − ab + ac − bc = 0: 90°

cards.term: Misc Q2: the equation of the line through the origin parallel to the x-axis.
cards.definition: Direction ratios of the x-axis: (1, 0, 0). x/1 = y/0 = z/0

cards.term: Misc Q3: if (x − 1)/(−3) = (y − 2)/(2k) = (z − 3)/2 and (x − 1)/(3k) = (y − 1)/1 = (z − 6)/(−5) are perpendicular, find k.
cards.definition: Directions (−3, 2k, 2) and (3k, 1, −5): −9k + 2k − 10 = 0: k = −10/7

cards.term: Misc Q4: shortest distance between r = 6î + 2ĵ + 2k̂ + λ(î − 2ĵ + 2k̂) and r = −4î − k̂ + μ(3î − 2ĵ − 2k̂).
Misc Q5: the vector equation of the line through (1, 2, −4) perpendicular to (x − 8)/3 = (y + 19)/(−16) = (z − 10)/7 and (x − 15)/3 = (y − 29)/8 = (z − 5)/(−5).
cards.definition: Direction = cross product of (3, −16, 7) and (3, 8, −5) = (24, 36, 72) = 12(2, 3, 6). r = î + 2ĵ − 4k̂ + λ(2î + 3ĵ + 6k̂)

cards.term: Do the lines (x − 1)/2 = (y − 2)/3 = (z − 3)/4 and (x − 4)/5 = (y − 1)/2 = z intersect?
cards.definition: Points: (1 + 2λ, 2 + 3λ, 3 + 4λ) and (4 + 5μ, 1 + 2μ, μ). From z: μ = 3 + 4λ. From y: 2 + 3λ = 1 + 2μ = 7 + 8λ, so λ = −1 and μ = −1. Check x: 1 − 2 = −1 and 4 − 5 = −1 ✓. They intersect at (−1, −1, −1)

cards.term: Foot of the perpendicular from a point to a line: method.
cards.definition: Take a general point on the line (from the parametric form), form the vector to the given point, and set its dot product with the direction to 0 to find λ. The distance is the length of that vector

cards.term: Distance of the point (x₀, y₀, z₀) from the line r = a + λb?
cards.definition: |b × (p − a)| / |b| where p is the position vector of the point

cards.term: Distance of the point (1, 2, 3) from the line through the origin with direction (1, 1, 1)?
Reflection of a point in a line: idea.
cards.definition: Find the foot F of the perpendicular; the image P′ satisfies F = midpoint of P and P′, so P′ = 2F − P

cards.term: The line joining (2, 3, 4) and (5, 6, 7): direction cosines?
cards.definition: Ratios (3, 3, 3): (1/√3, 1/√3, 1/√3) (the line is equally inclined to the axes)

cards.term: Equation of the z-axis in Cartesian form?
cards.definition: x/0 = y/0 = z/1 (direction ratios 0, 0, 1 through the origin)

cards.term: Equation of the line through (1, 2, 3) and (4, 6, 3)?
cards.definition: Direction (3, 4, 0): (x − 1)/3 = (y − 2)/4 = (z − 3)/0 (the line lies in the plane z = 3)

cards.term: When are two lines with equations in parametric form the same line?
cards.definition: When they share a point and their direction ratios are proportional
Ratios (2, 2, 1), magnitude 3: (a)

cards.term:
MCQ: the direction ratios of the line (x − 1)/2 = (y + 2)/3 = (z − 5)/(−1) are
(a) 2, 3, −1 (b) 1, −2, 5 (c) 2, 3, 1 (d) −1, 2, −5
cards.definition: (a) 2, 3, −1

cards.term:
MCQ: if a line has direction cosines (l, m, n) with l = m = n, then l =
(a) ±1/√3 (b) ±1/3 (c) ±1/2 (d) 1
cards.definition: (a)

cards.term:
MCQ: the angle between the lines with directions (1, 1, 0) and (0, 1, 1) is
(a) 60° (b) 30° (c) 90° (d) 45°
cards.definition: cos θ = 1/2: (a) 60°

cards.term:
MCQ: the lines with direction ratios (1, 2, 3) and (2, 4, 6) are
(a) parallel (b) perpendicular (c) skew (d) intersecting at 60°
cards.definition: (a) parallel

cards.term:
MCQ: the shortest distance between r = t(î + ĵ + k̂) and r = î + s(ĵ + k̂) is
(a) 1/√2 (b) 1 (c) 1/√3 (d) 0
cards.definition: Both lines pass through (1, 1, 1) (t = 1, s = 1), so they intersect: (d) 0

cards.term:
MCQ: the line r = î + λ(î + ĵ + k̂) passes through the point
(a) (2, 1, 1) (b) (2, 1, 0) (c) (1, 1, 1) (d) (0, 0, 0)
cards.definition: λ = 1 gives (2, 1, 1): (a)

cards.term:
MCQ: the distance between the parallel lines r = a + λb with a = (0, 0, 0) and a′ = (1, 0, 0), b = (0, 0, 1) is
(a) 1 (b) 0 (c) 2 (d) √2
Integer answer (JEE Main): the square of the shortest distance between the lines r = (1, 2, 3) + λ(1, 0, 0) and r = (0, 0, 0) + μ(0, 1, 0) is?
cards.definition: b₁ × b₂ = (0, 0, 1); (a₂ − a₁) · (0, 0, 1) = −3: d = 3, so d² = 9

cards.term: Integer answer: the direction ratios of a line are 2, −1, −2. What is 3l, where l is the first direction cosine (positive direction)?
cards.definition: Magnitude 3: l = 2/3, so 3l = 2

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: the direction cosines of a line satisfy l² + m² + n² = 1.
R: they are the components of a unit vector along the line.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (a)

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: two skew lines have a unique common perpendicular.
R: a line perpendicular to b₁ and b₂ is parallel to b₁ × b₂.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (a): the direction of the common perpendicular is fixed by b₁ × b₂

cards.term: True/False: two distinct lines with the same direction cosines must be parallel.
cards.definition: True

cards.term: True/False: direction ratios of a line are unique.
cards.definition: False: any non-zero multiple works

cards.term: 2-mark: find the direction cosines of the line joining (0, 0, 0) and (1, 2, 2).
cards.definition: Magnitude 3: (1/3, 2/3, 2/3)

cards.term: 2-mark: find the vector equation of the line through (1, 2, 3) with direction 2î − ĵ + k̂.
cards.definition: r = î + 2ĵ + 3k̂ + λ(2î − ĵ + k̂)

cards.term: 3-mark: find the angle between the lines (x − 1)/1 = (y − 2)/2 = (z − 3)/2 and x/2 = y/1 = z/2.
cards.definition: Directions (1, 2, 2), (2, 1, 2): dot = 8, magnitudes 3 and 3: cos θ = 8/9. θ = cos⁻¹(8/9)

cards.term: 3-mark: find the shortest distance between r = (î + ĵ) + λ(2î − ĵ + k̂) and r = (2î + ĵ − k̂) + μ(3î − 5ĵ + 2k̂).
4-mark: show that the lines (x − 1)/2 = (y − 2)/3 = (z − 3)/4 and (x − 4)/5 = (y − 1)/2 = z intersect and find the point.
cards.definition: Equate parametric values: λ = μ = −1 satisfies all three equations. Point (−1, −1, −1)

cards.term: 4-mark: find the foot of the perpendicular from (1, 2, 3) to the line through the origin with direction (1, 1, 1).
cards.definition: Foot F = t(1, 1, 1) with (1 − t, 2 − t, 3 − t) · (1, 1, 1) = 6 − 3t = 0 → t = 2: F = (2, 2, 2) and the distance = |(−1, 0, 1)| = √2

cards.term: Case-based: two aircraft fly along the lines r = (0, 0, 10) + t(1, 0, 0) and r = (0, 0, 0) + s(0, 1, 0) (positions in km). What is their minimum separation?
cards.definition: The common perpendicular direction is (0, 0, 1); the offset is (0, 0, 10): 10 km

cards.term: Case-based: a laser beam travels from A(0, 0, 0) along direction (1, 2, 2). How far from the beam is the point P(3, 0, 0)?
cards.definition: AP × b = (3, 0, 0) × (1, 2, 2) = (0, −6, 6), magnitude 6√2; |b| = 3: distance 2√2 units
